description: One-way ratchet on ESLint warnings, counted by scripts/run-lint.mjs from a single ESLint run. totals.warningCeiling is the exact measured count, may only fall, and is the value npm run lint enforces. perRule freezes each warning rule at its own count so a drawdown in one rule cannot silently pay for a regression in another. Lower a ceiling in the same change that removes warnings; leaving headroom lets it refill silently.

notes.errorCeiling: Zero and permanent. ESLint errors are not part of the warning drawdown.
notes.@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: 4753 = the 4755 in config/type-escape-boundaries.json minus its 2 suppressions, which are not an ESLint rule. The binding gate for this rule stays config/type-escape-boundaries.json, which freezes every file individually and is therefore strictly stronger than a repository total. This ceiling exists so the two cannot disagree - it must be lowered whenever the type-escape ceiling is.
notes.phase17: Phase 17 recorded 33 here - 28 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps and 5 no-control-regex - as the outcome of a fully cleaned tree. That tree did not land. PR #684 merged the number without the cleanup and with its own CI run cancelled, so every build since has failed this gate by more than five thousand, and a gate that always fails gates nothing. These values are the tree as it is actually measured. Against 9270, the last count this ratchet took from a real ESLint run, it is a 43% drawdown; against Phase 17's aspiration it reads as a rise. Phase 18 continues from the measured number. Do not raise it again.
